summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with diarrhea and a low-grade fever. He has a history of HCV cirrhosis, portopulmonary hypertension, and recent hospitalization for similar symptoms. Workup revealed no infectious cause for diarrhea, which was attributed to Remodulin therapy. Blood cultures grew Acinetobacter from his tunneled central line, leading to line removal, temporary central access, and a 14-day course of meropenem. A new PICC was successfully placed. He underwent therapeutic paracentesis for refractory ascites, with albumin administration. Diuretics were increased, and home medications adjusted. He improved clinically, completed antibiotic therapy, and was discharged home with plans to restart ciprofloxacin, monitor for infection clearance, and coordinate tunneled line replacement.
